title: What is Parkinson's Disease?
content: Parkinson's disease is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder involving dopamine-producing neurons in the brain. Symptoms usually develop gradually and can differ considerably from one person to another. Common movement symptoms include tremor, slowness of movement known as bradykinesia, rigidity, and gait or balance problems. Parkinson's can also cause non-movement symptoms involving areas such as mood, sleep and cognition. The presence of one symptom alone does not establish that a person has Parkinson's disease.
